title: Lightweight session provenance and metric primer for inference dashboards
summary: A concise, practitioner-focused reference for instrumenting session provenance, defining a minimal metric lexicon, and sketching compact dashboard panels that are low-cardinality and cost-aware for LLM inference products. Includes example trace anchors, payload conventions, and a rollout check-list for quick instrumentation during model swaps.
content:
Purpose
This doc is a pragmatic primer for engineers and product owners who need to ship lightweight observability for inference paths quickly. Focus: session provenance (reconstructing a user journey across multi-turn/chat/chain-of-calls), a small set of metric primitives that cover latency/cost/quality, and compact dashboard templates that minimize query cost and cardiality.

Why this exists (context)
- We repeatedly see investigation latency increase because sessions split across microcalls and model fanouts are hard to stitch.
- Full-fidelity traces are expensive to store/query; operators need a compact signal set and deterministic anchors to find the traces that matter.
- Dashboard sprawl and high-cardinality panels blow query budgets. This doc suggests minimal constructs to stay practical while being useful for oncall and postmortem.

Metric lexicon (minimal, with definitions and unit)
- session_id_probes: synthetic sessions per minute (count). Purpose: active synthetic checks scoped to critical models/endpoints.
- user_session_count: unique session IDs started per minute (count). Session ID = client_assigned_id OR server-generated (see provenance rules).
- request_p95_ms / request_p50_ms: latency from API auth to final token emission (milliseconds). Exclude queuing when measuring model compute SLOs where queue time is relevant.
- token_cost_usd_per_request: estimated cost in USD per request (derived at ingestion time using model, token_count, quant_profile). Unit: USD. Use this for budget heatmaps.
- kv_cache_hits: per-session KV cache hits (count). Important for customer-facing latency stories.
- fanout_model_count: number of distinct models called for a logical request (count). Monitors increased complexity.
- quality_regressions: alertable counter when eval-set rejection rate exceeds threshold (count). Hook to Redwood Optimize eval signals.
- error_class_{class}: short label-valued metric for high-level error taxonomy (e.g., model_oom, gateway_timeout, auth_fail). Use small set of enumerated values.

Session provenance rules (practical, deterministic)
- Session ID selection: prefer client-provided session_id header if signed and passes HMAC (server_key). Fallback: generate session_id = sha1(customer_id + client_ip + request_ts_minute) and mark as "generated".
- Span anchors: every public API request must emit a span with tags: session_id, route, customer_id (hashed), model_variant, and token_counts.{prompt,completion,total}. Keep tag values small.
- Correlation token: include a 12-byte correlation token in request/response headers that surfaces in logs and trace IDs. This token is opaque and maps to the trace sampling backend TTL.
- Multi-hop stitching: for internal fanouts, propagate the correlation token in x-rw-corr header; downstream services must log it and add a small span with "fanout_index" to indicate ordering.

Trace anchor patterns (how to find the trace you need quickly)
- Start from dashboard panel: click the row for session_id and route -> link should query traces by correlation token and time +/- 30s.
- For cold-cache incidents: look for session_id with kv_cache_hits==0 and request_p95_ms high; anchor trace on the first model call span.
- For hallucination/quality regressions: anchor on the web-hooked eval-result span (quality_regressions > threshold) and follow upstream correlation tokens to user session.

Payload and span size guidance
- Keep span annotations to < 10 simple key-values. Avoid entire prompt dumps in traces; instead emit prompt_hash and, if allowed, a short prompt_snippet (<= 160 chars) in traces. Full prompt storage should live in a separate prompt archive with access controls and only linked by prompt_hash.
- Token list suppression: do not include token arrays in traces. Use counts only.

Dashboard panel templates (compact, low-cardinality)
- SLO overview (single row per route): columns = route, p50_ms, p95_ms, error_rate_5m, token_cost_1h_avg. Use pre-aggregated hourly rollups in storage.
- Session warmth heatmap: x axis = hour, y axis = tenant_weight_bucket, value = user_session_count. This avoids per-tenant panels.
- Fanout complexity trend: timeseries of avg(fanout_model_count) per route. Annotate when model_variant changes.
- Cost hotlist: Top 10 session_ids by token_cost_usd_per_request in last 1h (cap rows to 10). Clicking row opens trace by correlation token.
- Compact trace list: table of correlation_token, route, duration_ms, kv_cache_hits, quality_flag. Link to full trace only for top signals.

Investigation flow (for operators)
1) Alert fires (source: SLO or quality_regressions). Open the SLO overview row for the route.
2) Check token_cost and kv_cache_hits. If kv_cache_hits is low and latency is high -> warm-up path.
3) Use cost hotlist to find heavy sessions and click to retrieve trace (correlation token).
4) If trace absent, escalate to retention policy owners; otherwise, inspect fanout spans for model OOMs or timeouts.

Rollout instrumentation quick-checklist (for model swaps / canary)
- Add synthetic session probes: at least 3 probes/min covering critical prompts.
- Emit early flag: model_rollout_id and model_variant tags on every span.
- Add eval hook: route-level eval-set checks that can flip quality_regressions metric.
- Ensure token_cost_usd_per_request is computable for new variant.
- Create a temporary dashboard slice: canary vs baseline p95/p50 + quality_regressions.

Privacy and retention notes
- Prompt content stored only when customer consent present. Traces must reference prompt_hash and not raw prompt.
- Correlation token TTL = 7 days for high-res traces; aggregated metrics longer in rollups.
- PHI/PII redaction: prompt_snippet must run a regex redactor before emission; if matched, replace snippet with "[REDACTED_SNIPPET]" and set quality_flag to review_needed.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Level of cardinality allowed for tenant tagging: hashed customer_id is useful but increases cardinality when combined with route/model. Proposal: only expose tenant-level metrics in on-call dashboards; avoid per-tenant timeseries except in dedicated dashboards.
- Trace retention vs. cost: suggest short TTL (7d) for full traces with extended index for correlation tokens (30d) pointing to rollup artifacts.
- Prompt archival: where to store prompt archive (S3 with KMS + audit). Depends on legal/compliance asks.

Implementation notes and snippets
- SQL snippet for SLO overview p95: SELECT route, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) AS p95_ms, countIf(status!='ok')/count(*) as error_rate_5m FROM inference_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '5' minute GROUP BY route ORDER BY p95_ms DESC LIMIT 50;
- Trace query example (link): /traces?corr_token={{correlation_token}}&from={{ts-30s}}&to={{ts+30s}}

Appendix: quick glossary
- correlation_token: short opaque id used to stitch microcalls.
- prompt_hash: sha256 of the normalized prompt used to reference archived prompt.
- kv_cache_hits: count of successful KV cache lookups in model runtime.

Next steps / action items
- [ ] Run a 2-week experiment where new model rollouts must populate these minimal tags (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add synthetic probes to Canary infra (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Draft retention policy for correlation_token and trace spans (owner: Marta).
- [ ] Review SLO overview SQL and add to the standard widgets library (owner: James).

Notes to reviewers
This is intentionally compact—aim is to get a usable set of signals into dashboards in a few days. Comments welcome on session ID generation heuristics and prompt archival constraints.
